correctness.rationale: Every valid inverse corresponds to an abba window. Equality of two resulting adjacent-pair deletions forces a two-periodic bridge; one window has adjacent equal central letters so the bridge is constant. Therefore only windows within a single long constant run collide. This gives the exact marked-run count; length budget and an alternating binary witness yield the sharp maximum; counting each nonconstant palindrome and long-run start yields the incidence sum. 59,420 independently enumerated received words pass the exact conditions; the proof, not the finite test, covers all q and m.

value.rationale: The inverse list is the actual decoder ambiguity under one fixed-span palindromic duplication. A complete run-based characterization provides linear-time exact list cardinalities; the sharp worst-case list size gives operational worst-case decoding cost; the exact q-ary incidence sum describes global channel multiplicity. The result answers a natural channel question with structural content rather than a small arbitrary parameter computation.
